correctness.rationale: For every even graph order, the period-two Fourier reduction gives an exact two-by-two block and the zero-mode eigenvalue 1-2c. The identity |Z|^2-(X-Y)^2=4Xd^2 sin^2(theta) proves Re sqrt(Z)>=c cos(theta), and equality is rigid for orders at least six. The two decreasing/increasing scalar envelope terms meet at the claimed unique c. At four vertices the nonzero block has radicand d^2-4r^2; equality exactly forces that radicand to vanish and c=2/3. A nonzero nilpotent two-by-two block proves the defective repeated root. Symbolic four- and six-state characteristic polynomials and 2275 finite samples were independently recomputed within the same review process; finite samples are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two-periodic edge heterogeneity is the simplest nonconstant symmetry class of an even cycle, and uniform circulation is the unique independent skew perturbation compatible with doubly stochastic cycle transitions. Their simultaneous optimization was not settled by the separate-direction published comparisons. The exact all-length threshold and uniqueness result are useful for design, while the exceptional defective four-state equality shows that optimal spectral radius can coexist with nonnormal transient behavior. This is a structural boundary rather than a renaming, one-step numerical gain, or arbitrary finite slice.
